title.en: Car-following waves on a closed single lane

summary: Simulate continuous car-following on a periodic lane and connect every vehicle's motion to its bumper gap, approaching rate and declared Intelligent Driver Model parameters.
objective: Perturb one vehicle on a closed lane and inspect how gaps, accelerations and speed waves evolve without intersections, lane changes or boundary inflow.
intent_signals: Show cars following one another on a circular single lane.
Perturb a ring-road platoon and inspect whether a speed disturbance grows or decays.
Explain each car's acceleration from speed, headway and relative speed.
example_prompts: Build an IDM ring road with 18 identical cars, a selectable headway arc and a speed-history cylinder.
Let me brake one car briefly, then inspect the resulting gap and speed wave on a closed lane.
negative_signals: Not route planning, signal control, intersection traffic, overtaking or lane changing.
Not a calibrated forecast of a named road or a vehicle collision engine.
not_for: Road-safety certification, autonomous-driving control or reconstruction of a real crash.
Inferring traffic capacity or stability for uncalibrated parameters from one animation.

entities.name: Closed lane and vehicles
entities.guidance: Build a single centerline loop of length L with lane-width context but no branches. Give every vehicle a visible front and rear bumper, stable ID, identical declared length by default, and ordered centerline coordinate q modulo L.

entities.name: Follower-leader inspection
entities.guidance: For the selected car, draw the forward bumper-to-bumper arc s to its leader, show v, leader speed, Delta v=v-v_leader, desired gap s-star and acceleration. Keep the wraparound leader link visible at the periodic seam.

entities.name: Space-time history
entities.guidance: Unwrap lane coordinate against time on a vertical panel or cylinder and plot vehicle traces plus a speed color legend. Height is model time; line brightness does not encode traffic flow unless explicitly calculated.

state_contract.model: For N>=2 fixed cyclic vehicle identities of length ell on a closed centerline of length L>N*ell, initialize unwrapped coordinates q_0<q_1<...<q_(N-1)<q_0+L and v_i>=0. Vehicle i<N-1 follows i+1 with s_i=q_(i+1)-q_i-ell; vehicle N-1 follows vehicle 0's next periodic image with s_(N-1)=q_0+L-q_(N-1)-ell. Delta v_i=v_i-v_leader. Modulo L is used only to map unwrapped q_i to rendered lane position, never to calculate a safety gap. With positive v0,a,b,T,s0 and exponent delta, use s-star=s0+v_i*T+v_i*Delta v_i/(2*sqrt(a*b)) and dv_i/dt=a*[1-(v_i/v0)^delta-(s-star/s_i)^2], dq_i/dt=v_i, matching the cited s1=0 IDM. Integrate all vehicles from one simultaneous state with declared tolerances and gap event functions. Before accepting each solver interval, detect whether any continuous gap reaches gap_epsilon or any speed reaches zero from above; terminate at the first located event and diagnose it rather than accepting an overtake, negative speed or overlap.
state_contract.authority: The simultaneous ODE state owns all vehicle transforms, gaps and histories. Wheel rotation, camera pursuit and interpolation never feed back into q or v. The circular mesh is parameterized by authoritative arclength, not used as a physics collider.
actions: Select a follower and inspect its leader, actual gap, desired gap, approaching rate and acceleration.
Apply a bounded, explicitly external deceleration pulse to one vehicle, then return control to the IDM and mark the intervention interval.
Change density by rebuilding an evenly spaced initial state with a valid L>N*ell configuration.
Play, pause, scrub and compare unperturbed and perturbed runs from identical parameters.
Reset vehicles, parameters, perturbation and model time.

invariants: Leader order and vehicle count remain fixed on the single closed lane: q_0<q_1<...<q_(N-1)<q_0+L throughout every accepted solver interval. A periodic seam changes rendered coordinates, not this unwrapped identity order.
The sum of all bumper gaps equals L-N*ell within arithmetic tolerance at every valid state.
Every acceleration is evaluated from the same time state before integration advances; sequentially moving cars would create order-dependent dynamics and is rejected.

Normal playback locates and stops at the first gap_epsilon or zero-speed crossing before accepting an interval that would overtake, overlap or become negative. The authored implementation does not claim that a finite-step integrator inherits a continuous model's collision-free analysis.
motion_guidance: Map q modulo L to the lane centerline while retaining unwrapped q for continuous histories and seam-crossing interpolation.
Derive wheel angle from traveled arclength with a declared visual radius. Wheel spin is display kinematics and carries no tire-force claim.
A brake pulse is an external input shown on the time history; do not hide it inside a changed desired speed.
creative_affordances: Use a compact proving ground, elevated urban loop or abstract traffic instrument, provided the lane remains single, closed and unbranched.
A vertical space-time curtain or cylindrical trace cage can make backward-propagating speed structures visible without claiming a three-dimensional roadway.
known_limits: Identical deterministic vehicles on one homogeneous lane omit reaction noise, lane changes, intersections, heterogeneous drivers, grade, signals and network demand.
IDM parameters require calibration for quantitative traffic claims. This recipe illustrates one equation set and does not guarantee that a chosen run reproduces empirical stop-and-go traffic.
Finite-step collision and negative-speed handling remain numerical responsibilities. No solver run, scene runtime or rendered observation has been executed for this draft.

claims.statement: Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing define continuous single-lane car-following acceleration from vehicle speed, bumper-to-bumper gap and approaching rate; their IDM equations (6)-(7), with s1 set to zero for the simple identical-vehicle case, combine free-road acceleration with a squared desired-gap interaction term, and their stability analysis includes homogeneous traffic on a circular road.
claims.scope: The deterministic IDM and circular-road analysis in the cited 2000 paper; not a claim that this draft's numerical implementation, parameters or finite-step playback is calibrated or collision-free.

source_refs.locator: Section II.1 equations (2)-(3); Section II.2 equations (6)-(7) and s1=0 paragraph; Section II.4 first paragraph

object_craft.structure: Low-poly cars have explicit front/rear faces, wheelbase cues and stable roof IDs; each sits on one shared centerline frame and retains a thin ground footprint for gap inspection.
object_craft.material: Neutral bodies with a selected outline and speed legend; brake lamps illuminate only during negative acceleration or the external pulse and are not collision sensors.
object_craft.articulation: Vehicle pose follows centerline arclength and tangent; front wheels need not steer on the authored kinematic path unless their visual steering is derived from centerline curvature.

object_craft.structure: A thin lane-following headway ribbon joins bumpers, while a separate unwrapped space-time panel carries one trace per stable vehicle ID and an intervention band.
object_craft.material: Gap safety thresholds use line style and numeric labels as well as color. History traces remain readable through periodic seam crossings.
object_craft.articulation: The selected ribbon and time cursor update from the simultaneous ODE state; the history panel grows only along model time.

physical_contract.scope: Longitudinal deterministic car-following along a prescribed periodic centerline; no rigid-body contact or steering dynamics.
physical_contract.timestep: Use one declared ODE integrator for the simultaneous state with continuous gap and zero-speed event checks on every accepted interval. Log tolerance or maximum step, and compare minimum gap and speed traces after tightening tolerance or halving maximum step.
state: leader identity and bumper gap s_i
colliders: Vehicle footprints are diagnostic envelopes only; they do not resolve contact.
driving: IDM longitudinal acceleration owns speed outside marked external intervention intervals.
Centerline mapping owns world pose and preserves periodic arclength.
contact: A located s_i=gap_epsilon event terminates normal playback before the interval is accepted; modulo rendering never hides an overtake and vehicles never pass through or reorder.
checks: Verify q_0<...<q_(N-1)<q_0+L and sum gaps=L-N*ell at every accepted output and event bracket.
Compare a uniform unperturbed run with the perturbed run under identical integration settings.
Repeat minimum-gap and speed extrema after tighter solver settings before interpreting a traffic wave.
